task_description: Designing novel alloy electrocatalyst surface structures with high activity and selectivity for the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), specifically by generating surfaces predicted to exhibit optimal CO adsorption energy (ΔECO ≈ −0.67 eV) while simultaneously satisfying constraints on hydrogen adsorption energy (to suppress HER) and thermodynamic stability (via formation energy).

datasets.db_description: A database of catalyst surfaces created by Tran et al., containing diverse surface structures used to pretrain the CDVAE generative model; it provides the structural foundation for generating new alloy surfaces and serves as the training data for both the CDVAE and the supervised DimeNet++ models predicting ΔECO and ΔEH, enabling property-guided inverse design of CO2RR-active surfaces.

The Open Quantum Materials Database, used to train the MEGNet model for predicting formation energy (Ef); this dataset provides thermodynamically stable inorganic compound structures and energies, allowing the framework to evaluate and filter generated surfaces for thermodynamic stability without performing costly DFT calculations.

A curated collection of 110 DFT-validated alloy surface structures generated by MAGECS and screened for CO2RR activity, selectivity, and stability; it contains DFT-calculated ΔECO, ΔEH, and formation energies, and was used to benchmark ML model accuracy and support experimental validation—serving as the final candidate set for synthesis and characterization.
